result:
Compilation succeeded. I wrote `tests/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVParserAgentTest.java` (package `org.apache.commons.csv`, JUnit 5/Jupiter) with 37 self-contained test methods covering `CSVParser`'s documented contract:

- All six static `parse(...)` factories (String, Reader, File, Path, InputStream, URL), including null-argument contracts (NPE vs. `IllegalArgumentException` per the javadoc's differing wording per overload) and null-format/null-charset defaulting behavior.
- Both deprecated constructors, including the inconsistent-format and null-reader/format `IllegalArgumentException` cases, and the record-number-offset constructor.
- `nextRecord()`, `getRecordNumber()`, `getCurrentLineNumber()` progression and null-at-EOF.
- `getRecords()` boundary cases (empty input, resuming from current position, `CSVFormat.Builder.setMaxRows`), plus quoted/multiline value parsing.
- `getHeaderMap()` (copy semantics), `getHeaderMapRaw()`, `getHeaderNames()` (read-only list).
- Header/trailer comment detection (`hasHeaderComment`/`hasTrailerComment` before and after full consumption).
- `getFirstEndOfLine()` for both `\n` and `\r\n`.
- `isClosed()`/`close()` idempotency, and `iterator()`/`stream()` end-of-data and post-close behavior.

One notable constraint I discovered: `lib/` doesn't include `commons-io`, and `CSVParser.Builder`/`CSVParser.builder()...` chains extend commons-io's `AbstractStreamBuilder`, so any call touching its inherited members (`setReader`, etc.) fails to compile. I avoided that API entirely (using the deprecated constructors and static `parse` methods instead, which are self-contained) and only verified `CSVParser.builder()` itself returns a non-null instance.
